title: 'It makes me feel that we can do a lot about it': ESA official shares striking satellite snap of Europe's record-breaking summer heat waves
summary: The head of ESA's Earth observation program tells Live Science why a striking image of a recent heat wave scorching Southern Europe gives her hope that we can properly monitor ‪— and eventually prevent ‪— similar extreme weather events in the future.
body: QUICK FACTS Where is it? Southern Europe and North Africa What's in the photo? Land and sea surface temperatures during one of Europe's record-breaking summer heat waves Which satellite took the photo? Sentinel-3B When was it taken? June 23, 2026 This striking satellite snap shows the scorching land and sea surface temperatures that hit Southern Europe during one of the continent's record-breaking heat waves this summer. The image was created using data from the Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer (SLSTR) on board the European Space Agency's (ESA) Sentinel-3B satellite. It was selected for this week's edition of Earth from space by Simonetta Cheli , director of Earth observation programs at ESA and head of the European Space Research Institute (ESRIN) in Frascati, Italy. Live Science recently visited Frascati to see ESRIN's newly operational Space HPC supercomputer and sat down with Cheli for an in-depth discussion about Earth observation . When asked about her favorite satellite image, Cheli highlighted this photo as one that caught her eye this year. In the thermal image, dark reds highlight terrestrial temperatures in excess of 95 degrees Fahrenheit (35 degrees Celsius)…
